detail:
A 2025 review of gastric peroral endoscopic myotomy (G-POEM) describes it as a minimally invasive, pylorus-directed intervention for gastroparesis that remains symptomatic despite dietary and medical therapy. Across studies, technical success consistently exceeds 95%, short-term symptom improvement is reported in up to 80% of patients, and longer-term clinical success ranges from about 50% to 77.5% at 3 to 4 years, influenced by the underlying cause.

The review compares G-POEM with botulinum toxin injection, gastric electrical stimulation, and surgical pyloroplasty, and highlights an open research question: predicting who will benefit. A functional imaging tool (EndoFLIP) that measures pyloric distensibility has shown promise for identifying candidates and assessing the procedure's effect, though standardized predictive thresholds are still lacking.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about whether any procedure research applies to your situation.
sourceVideoTitle: Redefining the Treatment Landscape in Gastroparesis: A Clinical Review of Gastric Peroral Endoscopic Myotomy Outcomes and Therapeutic Integration
summary: A 2025 clinical review reports that G-POEM, an endoscopic procedure that opens the stomach's outlet muscle, achieves technical success above 95% and short-term symptom improvement in up to 80% of carefully selected patients whose gastroparesis has not responded to standard care.
takeaways: g-poem targets the pylorus in refractory cases only
long-term success in studies ranges from about 50 to 78 percent
imaging tools are being tested to pick the best candidates
procedures are specialist decisions after standard care falls short
title: Gastroparesis research: pylorus-focused procedures
